page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-800s-amd is an instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a memory-heavy ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The setup provides 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache. Alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, the instance bundles 800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance achieved 3132.97, placing it in the top 10% tier, corroborated by a strong Geekbench single-core score of 1996.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks placed uncached read (228.44 GB/sec) and write operations (156.49 GB/sec) into the top 25% bracket, matching a solid PassMark memory score of 2876.37. Multi-threaded workloads show stable mid-range performance, with multi-core stress-ng at 25046.38, Geekbench multi-core at 9998.0, and PassMark CPU score at 20591.17. Compression tasks, static web serving (7.46 GB/sec), and in-memory key-value processing via Redis (19.03 million SET operations/sec) all sustained consistent middle-tier scores.

The primary tradeoff stems from its compute density and lack of AVX-512 extensions. While single-thread execution is responsive, the 4-physical-core count limits throughput on compute-dense multithreaded tasks, as evidenced by lower-tier prompt processing for 7B parameter models (24.79 tokens/sec). However, the generous 64.0 GB RAM allocation combined with 800 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-demanding stateful applications. It is particularly effective for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data caching layers, enterprise backend services, and intermediate ETL staging.
description: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-800s-amd is an AMD EPYC x86_64 server within the Optimized Cloud Compute series, provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores at 2.0 GHz), 64.0 GB RAM, and 800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking a GPU, it focuses on memory capacity with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Single-threaded performance reaches top tiers, registering 3132.97 in stress-ng and 1996.0 in Geekbench, backed by strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 228 GB/sec for reads and 156 GB/sec for writes. Multi-core compute yields steady midrange scores across PassMark (20591.17) and Geekbench (9998.0). With 19.03 million Redis SET operations per second and high-capacity fast storage, it provides efficient operational capacity for in-memory databases, caching, and mid-sized transactional systems.
